1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""The builder: a cold session that changes a checkout until its tests pass.
3	
4	    uv run builder.py <checkout> "<goal>"
5	
6	The checkout is the directory named on the command line, reachable only through five tools:
7	list, read, write, edit and check. Writes are confined to the checkout and refused on the goal's
8	tests and the toolchain; check runs the checkout's tests in a container with no network and the
9	checkout mounted read-only, so code the model writes never runs on the host and cannot reach the
10	key. The loop is pydantic-ai, pinned; the provider is DeepSeek's chat completions API, the key
11	read from ~/.config/factory/deepseek.key and never written anywhere. Each run leaves
12	runs/<utc-stamp>/ under the factory itself, never in the checkout, with goal.txt, wire.jsonl
13	(every HTTP attempt as it happened), messages.json (the library's messages), check-<n>.log per
14	check, diff.patch (what the run left in the checkout; absent when it left nothing), report.json,
15	response.md (the report rendered) and numbers.json.
16	"""

102	class BuildReport(BaseModel):
103	    """The builder's report: what it changed in the checkout, and whether the tests pass."""
104	
105	    changed: list[str] = Field(description="The paths you wrote or edited, in order.")
106	    did: list[str] = Field(
107	        description="What you changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path."
108	    )
109	    check: Literal["green", "red"] = Field(description="Green or red: the state of the last check.")
110	    failing: list[str] = Field(description="Test names if red.")

115	            ("Failing", "failing"), ("Unsure", "unsure"))  # fmt: skip

119	    """The report in v0.1's markdown shape: five headings, one bullet per item."""
120	    out: list[str] = []
121	    for heading, field in SECTIONS:
122	        out.append(f"## {heading}")
123	        items = getattr(report, field)
124	        if isinstance(items, str):  # check is one value, and renders as one bullet
125	            items = [items]

127	        out.append("")

132	    """The tools: what the model can do to the checkout, and the record of it."""
133	
134	    def __init__(self, root: Path, run_dir: Path, hidden: tuple[str, ...] = HIDDEN,
135	                 protected: tuple[str, ...] = PROTECTED, sandbox: Any = None):  # fmt: skip
136	        self.root = root.resolve()
137	        self.run_dir = run_dir
138	        self.hidden = hidden
139	        self.protected = protected
140	        self.sandbox = sandbox
141	        self.listed: list[str] = []
142	        self.read_paths: list[str] = []
143	        self.lines_read = 0
144	        self.written: list[str] = []
145	        self.edited: list[str] = []
146	        self.checks: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

148	    def _resolve(self, path: str) -> tuple[Path, str]:
149	        p = (self.root / (path or ".")).resolve()
150	        if p != self.root and self.root not in p.parents:
151	            raise ValueError(f"outside the checkout: {path}")
152	        rel = p.relative_to(self.root).as_posix() or "."
153	        parts = rel.split("/")
154	        # A .git component at any depth is git's, not the checkout's: a write there could forge a
155	        # nested repository and hide a subtree from the record. The other hidden names are only
156	        # the record at the root.
157	        if parts[0] in self.hidden or ".git" in parts or ".git" in path.split("/"):
158	            raise ValueError(f"not part of the checkout: {path}")
159	        return p, rel
160	
161	    def _writable(self, rel: str) -> None:
162	        """The goal's tests and the toolchain are the human's; the builder may read them only."""
163	        name = rel.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
164	        for pattern in self.protected:
165	            if pattern.endswith("/"):  # anything under that directory
166	                hit = rel == pattern[:-1] or rel.startswith(pattern)
167	            elif "*" in pattern:  # that basename glob, anywhere in the checkout
168	                hit = fnmatch.fnmatchcase(name, pattern)
169	            elif pattern.startswith("."):  # that dotted basename, anywhere in the checkout
170	                hit = name == pattern
171	            else:  # that exact path at the root, not the basename anywhere
172	                hit = rel == pattern
173	            if hit:
174	                raise ValueError(
175	                    f"protected: {rel} (not the builder's to change: the tests, the toolchain, "
176	                    "the vault and git's own files)"
177	                )
178	
179	    def _capped(self) -> str:
180	        if len(self.written) + len(self.edited) >= WRITE_CAP:
181	            return f"error: cap reached ({WRITE_CAP} writes and edits); report now"
182	        return ""
183	
184	    def list(self, path: str = ".") -> str:
185	        """List one directory of the checkout: one entry per line as kind, size, name. Path is the
186	        directory to list, relative to the checkout root; '.' is the root.
187	
188	        Args:
189	            path: The directory to list, relative to the checkout root.
190	        """
191	        try:
192	            p, rel = self._resolve(path)
193	            if not p.is_dir():
194	                raise ValueError(f"not a directory: {path}")
195	            entries = sorted(p.iterdir(), key=lambda e: (not e.is_dir(), e.name))
196	            skip = self.hidden if rel == "." else (".git",)  # git's own files are never listed
197	            entries = [e for e in entries if e.name not in skip]
198	            lines = []
199	            for e in entries[:LIST_CAP]:
200	                kind = "link" if e.is_symlink() else "dir" if e.is_dir() else "file"
201	                size = e.lstat().st_size if kind == "file" else 0
202	                name = e.name if rel == "." else f"{rel}/{e.name}"  # paths from the checkout root
203	                lines.append(f"{kind}\t{size}\t{name}")
204	            if len(entries) > LIST_CAP:
205	                lines.append(f"...\t{len(entries) - LIST_CAP} more entries not shown")
206	        except (ValueError, OSError, RuntimeError) as e:  # RuntimeError: a symlink loop
207	            return f"error: {e}"
208	        self.listed.append(rel)
209	        return "\n".join(lines) or "(empty)"
210	
211	    def read(self, path: str, start: int = 1) -> str:
212	        """Read a file of the checkout as numbered lines, from line `start` (1-based), at most 300
213	        lines or 32000 bytes per call; a truncated read says where to continue.
214	
215	        Args:
216	            path: The file to read, relative to the checkout root.
217	            start: The first line to read, 1-based.
218	        """
219	        try:
220	            p, rel = self._resolve(path)
221	            if not p.is_file():
222	                raise ValueError(f"not a file: {path}")
223	            start = max(1, int(start))
224	            out: list[str] = []
225	            n = nbytes = 0
226	            with p.open("r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
227	                for i, line in enumerate(f, 1):
228	                    if i < start:
229	                        continue
230	                    size = len(line.encode())
231	                    if n >= READ_LINES_CAP or nbytes + size > READ_BYTES_CAP:
232	                        if n:  # one line per call at least, or a long line dead-ends the read
233	                            out.append(f"...\ttruncated; continue with start={i}")
234	                            break
235	                        cut = line.encode()[:READ_BYTES_CAP].decode("utf-8", "ignore")
236	                        out.append(f"{i}\t{cut} …(line cut at {READ_BYTES_CAP} bytes)")
237	                    else:
238	                        out.append(f"{i}\t{line.rstrip(chr(10))}")
239	                    n += 1
240	                    nbytes += size
241	        except (ValueError, OSError, RuntimeError) as e:  # RuntimeError: a symlink loop
242	            return f"error: {e}"
243	        self.read_paths.append(rel)
244	        self.lines_read += n
245	        return "\n".join(out) or "(empty)"

247	    def write(self, path: str, content: str) -> str:
248	        """Write a file of the checkout: create it, or replace what is there with `content`.
249	        Directories on the way are created. The tests and the toolchain cannot be written.
250	
251	        Args:
252	            path: The file to write, relative to the checkout root.
253	            content: The whole text of the file, as it should be afterwards.
254	        """
255	        capped = self._capped()
256	        if capped:
257	            return capped

266	        return f"wrote {rel} ({len(content.splitlines())} lines)"

276	            new: The text to put in its place.

281	        if not old:  # every file contains the empty string, everywhere

301	
302	    def check(self) -> str:
303	        """Run the checkout's tests and return the exit code and the tail of the output: exit 0 is
304	        green, anything else is red. The tests run in a container, with the checkout read-only and
305	        no network, so this reports on the checkout as it is on disk. At most 8 checks per run.
306	        """
307	        if len(self.checks) >= CHECK_CAP:
308	            return f"error: cap reached ({CHECK_CAP} checks); report now"
309	        if self.sandbox is None:
310	            return "error: no sandbox; check is not available in this run"
311	        n = len(self.checks) + 1
312	        t0 = time.time()
313	        try:
314	            code, output = self.sandbox.run(self.root, self.run_dir, n)
315	            seconds = round(time.time() - t0, 1)
316	            log = self.run_dir / f"check-{n}.log"
317	            log.write_text(output, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
318	        except (OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as e:
319	            return f"error: {e}"
320	        self.checks.append({"exit": code, "seconds": seconds})
321	        tail = "\n".join(output.splitlines()[-CHECK_TAIL_LINES:])
322	        if len(tail.encode()) > CHECK_TAIL_BYTES:  # the end of the output is the part that says why
323	            tail = tail.encode()[-CHECK_TAIL_BYTES:].decode("utf-8", "ignore")
324	        return f"exit {code}\n{tail}"
325	
326	
327	class Sandbox:
328	    """Where the checkout's tests run: a container, no network, the checkout mounted read-only.
329	
330	    The only place that knows about Docker. The image is the checkout's own locked dependencies,
331	    built once per (uv.lock, check.Dockerfile) pair and reused by every run afterwards.
332	    """
333	
334	    @staticmethod
335	    def image(checkout: Path) -> str:
336	        """The image name for this checkout: what it locks and how it is built, hashed."""
337	        h = hashlib.sha256((checkout / "uv.lock").read_bytes() + (checkout / "check.Dockerfile").read_bytes())
338	        return f"factory-check:{h.hexdigest()[:12]}"
339	
340	    @staticmethod
341	    def ensure_image(checkout: Path, run_dir: Path) -> str:
342	        """Build the image if it is not there yet; the build is the one step with network."""
343	        name = Sandbox.image(checkout)
344	        seen = subprocess.run(["docker", "image", "inspect", name], capture_output=True)
345	        if seen.returncode == 0:
346	            return name
347	        built = subprocess.run(
348	            # -f absolute: docker resolves a relative -f against the caller's directory, and the
349	            # factory never runs from inside the checkout.
350	            ["docker", "build", "-f", str(checkout / "check.Dockerfile"), "-t", name, str(checkout)],
351	            capture_output=True,
352	            timeout=IMAGE_TIMEOUT,
353	        )
354	        (run_dir / "image-build.log").write_bytes(built.stdout + built.stderr)
355	        if built.returncode != 0:
356	            raise RuntimeError(f"docker build failed (exit {built.returncode}); see image-build.log")
357	        return name
358	
359	    @staticmethod
360	    def run(checkout: Path, run_dir: Path, n: int) -> tuple[int, str]:
361	        """The checkout's tests, once: the exit code and everything the run printed."""
362	        name = Sandbox.ensure_image(checkout, run_dir)
363	        container = f"factory-check-{run_dir.name}-{n}"
364	        argv = [
365	            "docker", "run", "--rm", "--name", container,
366	            "--network", "none",  # the check cannot reach the key, the provider or the internet
367	            "--user", f"{os.getuid()}:{os.getgid()}",
368	            "-e", "HOME=/tmp",
369	            "-e", "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1",  # the checkout is read-only; do not try to cache
370	            "-v", f"{checkout}:/w:ro", "-w", "/w",
371	            "--memory", "1g", "--cpus", "2", "--pids-limit", "256",
372	            name, *CHECK_CMD,
373	        ]  # fmt: skip
374	        try:
375	            done = subprocess.run(argv, capture_output=True, timeout=CHECK_TIMEOUT)
376	        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
377	            try:  # the check is over either way; a wedged daemon must not hang the run too
378	                subprocess.run(["docker", "kill", container], capture_output=True, timeout=30)
379	            except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
380	                pass
381	            return 124, f"timeout after {CHECK_TIMEOUT} s"
382	        # unittest writes to stderr; the checkout's own code may write to either.
383	        return done.returncode, (done.stdout + done.stderr).decode("utf-8", "replace")

389	class Wire:
390	    """The raw HTTP record: one line per attempt, request and response, with no secret in it."""
391	
392	    def __init__(self, path: Path, transport: Any = None):
393	        self.path = path
394	        self.attempts = 0
395	        path.touch()
396	        self.client = httpx2.AsyncClient(
397	            transport=transport,
398	            event_hooks={"request": [self.on_request], "response": [self.on_response]},
399	        )
400

work around a failing test by changing what it asserts; no commentary outside the report.

1	# factory
2	
3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the checkout, until the checkout's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first checkout: since v0.3 its code is written by `builder.py` itself, from tests written before each build, and v0.4 is the first version made that way. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the tools, by the gate and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run gate.py check                                               # the vault against its templates and the repository; silent when they agree
13	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
14	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
15	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
16	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
17	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
18	uv run runs.py | tail -3                                           # the last run records, as rows of the table
19	```
20	
21	Then derive:
22	
23	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag; there is at most one. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
24	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `rejected`: a way out at any stage. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires and the gate checks it; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
25	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`. The gate's is `test_gate.py`.
26	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, `head`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and the wire, `wire.jsonl` fresh from a build and `wire.jsonl.gz` once committed. `uv run runs.py` is every record's numbers as one table. The commit that took the diff names the run in its `Built-By` trailer, so the builds of a version are `git log --format='%h %(trailers:key=Built-By,valueonly)' tags/<previous>..tags/<version>`, and the run's `head` is the red commit it started from.
27	
28	## How a version is made
29	
30	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` from the main checkout with that worktree as the checkout and the seed's goal as the goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, copies the record into the worktree, compresses its wire to `wire.jsonl.gz`, commits both as the factory's work, and hands the diff to an independent reviewer, a fresh session in this harness that reads the Goal, the diff and the tests and probes the change in throwaway directories; a defect the review finds, once the attended agent has verified it, becomes a test and a follow-up build on the same seed. When every seed of the version is done, the attended agent revises this file, writes the version note's changelog, fast-forwards `main` and runs `uv run gate.py release <version>`: the gate refuses until everything derived agrees, then cuts the annotated tag and renders `CHANGELOG.md`. The attended agent does not write code the factory could write and does not touch a test to make a build pass, because the factory's ability to do it is what is being measured; the tools refuse the model the same.
31	
32	## Commands
33	
34	- `uv run gate.py check`, `uv run gate.py render`, `uv run gate.py release <version>`: the gate. Problems go to stdout, one per line, starting with the path; exit 1 when there is any, 2 for a usage error, silence and 0 otherwise. `render` writes `CHANGELOG.md`. `release` also needs a clean tree, `AGENTS.md` changed since the previous tag, a green suite and at least one changelog bullet in the version note.
35	- `uv run python -m unittest -v`: the factory's own tests. Nothing external is needed.
